scenarios: a repository's .mcp.json declares a server whose command writes a marker file when it starts, a Claude command runs rm -rf when expanded and a profile asks for every permission
imported: the command and the profile are SKIPPED with reasons, the server is MAPPED and shown with its command line
loaded: the import is unsigned so the extension is quarantined; neither external.list nor an external.call naming the server starts it and the marker does not appear
trusted by the person: the listing starts the server and the marker appears
audit: NOT-FOUND before: nothing held another agent's executable configuration inert; only one Claude agent file could be converted.
proof: Real Core: imported executable configuration becomes an unsigned extension that is quarantined on load; its MCP server does not start until the person trusts it, and a command that runs shell or a profile that asks for authority is not imported at all.
negative_proof: Mutation: loading an import without quarantine fails the test (the marker appears before trust).
limitations: As IMP-EV-0183: TOML commands and non-stdio MCP servers are skipped by name; @file imports are not followed.

ci.note: every job green on macOS, Linux and Windows on attempt 2; attempt 1 failed only the desktop E2E jobs (states.spec 'approved at offset' on Linux, the browser-takeover spec on Windows), the known flakes this change does not touch; one change carries IMP-EV-0137 and IMP-EV-0183
